terms.meaning: a set of 3D objects, lights and a camera that the browser draws.
a picture where each point records how far away it is, used to lift a flat image into 3D.
one of the four modes the room can show, such as the interface or the videos.

sections.name: File setup, VaultView
sections.title: Design notes and view names
sections.what: Explains the vault design in a header comment and defines the four views: overview, interface, architecture and media.
sections.why: Records the intent: each build is a room with three walls of content.
sections.watch_out: The view names are also used by the page, so renaming one needs changes in both files.

sections.name: StackGraph
sections.title: Codebase graph shape
sections.what: Describes the data for the codebase wall: a source label, layers, technology nodes, the links between them, and the AI features.
sections.why: Gives the left wall one fixed shape to draw from, so every build's stack is drawn the same way.
sections.watch_out: Missing fields in the data will break the drawing, so check the data against this shape.

sections.name: VaultCallbacks
sections.title: Messages the scene sends out
sections.what: Lists the signals the 3D vault sends to the page around it: hovering over a room, entering a room, changing view, loading a codebase diagram, and moving between captures. It also holds the size constants for rooms, such as width, height, depth and spacing.
sections.why: Lets the page update its text and controls without the 3D code needing to know about them.
sections.watch_out: The room size constants drive every room, the camera framing and the background lattice together, so one change reshapes the whole scene.

sections.name: WARM
sections.title: Warm colour palette
sections.what: Six fixed colours, ranging from amber and brown to cream and steel blue, used for the vault's lines, light beams, dust and diagrams.
sections.why: Gives the vault one consistent warm look. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Other code refers to these colours by position (0, 2 and 4), so reordering the list changes the colours of graphs and shelves.

sections.name: rng
sections.title: Repeatable random number maker
sections.what: Creates a pseudo-random sequence from a starting number, so the same starting number always gives the same pattern.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the shelf and light layout identical on every visit.
sections.watch_out: The numbers depend on the order they are drawn, so reordering the calls changes the layout.

sections.name: Room
sections.title: Shape of one room record
sections.what: Describes everything kept for one room: its build, position, click target, moment ids, codebase and media parts once loaded, screens, and a glow value.
sections.why: Keeps each room's state in one place so parts can be added and removed as a visitor moves around.
sections.watch_out: Codebase and media groups exist only while a room is entered, so check they are present before using them.

sections.name: VaultScene (part 1)
sections.title: Scene setup and state fields
sections.what: Declares the vault's parts and state, including the renderer, camera, rooms, pointer tracking, current view, timers and label lists. The constructor creates the drawing surface, caps the pixel density at 2 (or 1.5 on low-power devices), and adds an overlay for lines.
sections.why: Keeps everything the scene needs to draw and respond to input in one class.
sections.watch_out: The pixel density cap is what keeps very sharp screens from slowing down, so raising it costs speed.

sections.name: VaultScene: for
sections.title: Building the vault and starting the loop
sections.what: Finishes setup: creates six tag markers, lays out the rooms, builds the background lattice, moments and light, sizes the view, and starts the animation loop. Work rooms sit in a four-column grid, and fun rooms sit to the right on wide screens or below on phones.
sections.why: Builds everything once so the scene is ready as soon as it appears.
sections.watch_out: The phone or wide layout is chosen once when the scene starts, so resizing the window later does not rearrange the rooms.

sections.name: VaultScene: addRoom
sections.title: Creating one room
sections.what: Adds a single room: an invisible clickable box for picking, anchor points where its captures attach, and a floating name label. It also starts drawing the warm lines on the room's walls.
sections.why: Each room needs something to click, a place for its captures, and a label.
sections.watch_out: Click boxes, labels and room records are matched by index number, so the index must stay consistent with the room list.

sections.name: VaultScene (part 4)
sections.title: Room frames, light beams and dust
sections.what: Draws the outline of each room's opening and back wall, the shared wall-line drawing, and the light beams that fall through each room. It also sets up the floating dust.
sections.why: Gives the rooms depth and atmosphere. Partly explained by the comments in the code.
sections.watch_out: Low-power mode uses fewer beams and dust particles, so the scene looks denser on some devices than others.

sections.name: VaultScene (part 5)
sections.title: Dust and one moment per capture
sections.what: Finishes the floating dust, then creates one palace moment for each capture. A capture is the screenshot shown in a room, or a generated spec sheet when the build has no screenshot.
sections.why: Each capture has to exist as a 3D item that the memory layer can show.
sections.watch_out: The spec sheet reads category, type and tags from project data, so missing values there will leave blank rows or fail.

sections.name: VaultScene: loadGraph
sections.title: Fetching a codebase diagram
sections.what: When a room is entered, downloads that project's stack file and prepares its diagram, reporting the result to the page. The result is dropped if the visitor has already left that room.
sections.why: Loads each diagram only when its room is viewed, which keeps the page light.
sections.watch_out: If the stack file is missing or fails to load, the diagram quietly does not appear and no error is shown.

sections.name: VaultScene (part 7)
sections.title: Drawing the diagram lines and labels
sections.what: Draws the diagram on the left wall: framed sections, a cloud of points for each node, curved lines between linked nodes, and on-screen labels for sections and nodes.
sections.why: Turns a project's structure into a visible map inside its room.
sections.watch_out: Node clouds are drawn with random numbers, so their exact shape changes on each visit, and links to unknown nodes are skipped without a message.

sections.name: VaultScene (part 8)
sections.title: Building video screens on the right wall
sections.what: Builds a frame for each video slot on the right wall. A slot with a video plays it muted and looping; an empty slot shows a flickering static texture with an awaiting file status.
sections.why: Gives every project a place for its videos and a visible placeholder when a file is missing.
sections.watch_out: Video playback failures are ignored, so a blocked video shows nothing and gives no error.

sections.name: VaultScene (part 9)
sections.title: Screen labels and clearing a room
sections.what: Finishes the screen labels, then clears a room by removing its diagram and video parts, pausing its videos, and freeing their graphics memory. It also contains two small helpers: one starts a smooth camera glide, and one cancels pending timed steps.
sections.why: Leaving a room must free memory and stop video so the page stays fast.
sections.watch_out: Clearing is the only place those parts are released, so any new part added to a room must also be released here.

sections.name: VaultScene: showWing
sections.title: Showing a wing and entering a room
sections.what: Frames the camera on the work wing, the fun wing, or all rooms. Entering a room first closes any other open room, then loads its diagram and screens and starts its capture walk-through.
sections.why: This is how a visitor moves between the overview and a single room.
sections.watch_out: The camera distance is calculated from the screen's shape, so the framing differs on tall and wide screens.

sections.name: VaultScene (part 11)
sections.title: Stepping through a capture
sections.what: Finishes the timed steps of a capture's walk-through, then switches between views such as architecture and media, moves to another capture, and returns to the overview when a room is left.
sections.why: Lets visitors explore a room at their own pace, from several angles.
sections.watch_out: Timed steps are queued with timers, and switching views cancels them, so a walk-through can stop partway.

sections.name: VaultScene: current
sections.title: Mouse input and picking rooms
sections.what: Tracks the pointer and which room it is over. A click picks the room under the pointer and enters it, unless a room is already open. It also keeps the scene sized to the window and recalculates the overview camera distance on resize.
sections.why: Lets visitors hover and click rooms in 3D by converting mouse position into a 3D target.
sections.watch_out: Clicks are ignored while a room is open, so the way out of a room must be handled elsewhere.

sections.name: VaultScene (part 13)
sections.title: The animation loop
sections.what: Runs on every frame: moves the camera along any glide, adds a small drift that follows the pointer, updates the glow of lines, dust and screens, draws the scene, and places labels. It also includes a helper that converts a 3D point into screen coordinates, and it pauses when the vault is scrolled out of view.
sections.why: This is the heartbeat that keeps the scene moving and responding to input.
sections.watch_out: Everything here runs on every frame, so any new per-frame work adds cost to the whole scene.

sections.name: VaultScene: drawLabels
sections.title: Placing labels over the scene
sections.what: Positions the room name labels on screen and shows them only when no room is open. Inside a room, it shows the diagram labels or screen labels for the current view, plus the tag numbers on the lifted capture.
sections.why: Keeps readable text attached to the 3D objects it describes.
sections.watch_out: Labels appear only after the camera glide is mostly finished, so a stalled glide can keep them hidden.

sections.name: VaultScene (part 15)
sections.title: Connecting tags and cleaning up
sections.what: Draws the lines joining the visible capture tags. The cleanup routine stops the loop and frees videos, graphics memory, labels and event listeners when the vault is removed.
sections.why: Prevents leftover memory use and stray events after visitors leave the page.
sections.watch_out: Anything added to the scene later must also be removed in this cleanup, or it will leak memory.

summary: The 3D engine for the AI builds vault. Only its header and data shapes were reviewed, so most of its behaviour is unclear from this part.
purpose: Draws each build as a room with an interface capture, a codebase wall and video screens.
why: The header comment says the design is a memory-palace style room, lit like the tesseract in the film Interstellar.
how: Reviewed part only: it defines four views (overview, interface, architecture and media) and the shape of the codebase graph. The rest of the steps are unclear from this part.
inputs: The build list, video slot list, asset paths, and a memory-layer helper from another folder. Other inputs are unclear from this part.
risks: Heavy 3D work, so an error here can blank the whole section. Other risks are unclear from this part.
debug: Start with the browser console. Then check that the interface capture, the graph data and the video files exist.
